docs.title: retrosheetpy
docs.text:
Fast, strongly-typed Retrosheet baseball data downloader, parser, and database ingestor.

retrosheetpy brings modern data workflows to Retrosheet baseball archives. It enables baseball researchers, analysts, professors, and DBAs to download, parse, and ingest play-by-play events, historical game logs, rosters, and ballparks directly into DuckDB, Parquet, Polars, pandas, and SQL databases with strongly-typed schemas (integers, dates, booleans—never raw text dumps).

Downloads default to the fast, rate-limit-free GitHub Fastly raw CDN mirror (chadwickbureau/retrosheet) with automatic fallback to retrosheet.org. Powered by chadwickpy for multi-core play-by-play parsing with zero C compiler dependencies.

docs.title: Unified Ingestion & Querying
docs.text:
One API to download, parse, and stream baseball data into your favorite analytical stack:

DuckDBPolars DataFramepandas DataFrameParquet / PyArrowPostgreSQL & dltSQL DDL 
import retrosheetpy as rs

# Ingest 2020 through 2024 into a local embedded analytical database
rs.to_duckdb(
    path="baseball.duckdb",
    years=range(2020, 2025),
    datasets=["events", "gamelogs", "rosters", "parks"],
)

import retrosheetpy as rs

# Blazing-fast play-by-play events in Polars
events_2024 = rs.events(year=2024, backend="polars")
print(events_2024.select(["GAME_ID", "BAT_ID", "PIT_ID", "EVENT_TX"]))

import retrosheetpy as rs

# 1871-present historical game logs
gl = rs.game_logs(year=2024, backend="pandas")
print(gl[["date", "visiting_team", "visiting_score", "home_team", "home_score"]].head())

import retrosheetpy as rs

# Export compressed columnar Parquet files
rs.to_parquet("gamelogs_1990_2024.parquet", dataset="gamelogs", years=range(1990, 2025))

import retrosheetpy as rs

# Stream multi-season datasets directly into PostgreSQL or Snowflake
rs.to_dlt(
    destination="postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/retrosheet",
    years=[2023, 2024],
    datasets=["rosters", "parks", "gamelogs"],
    dataset_name="public",
)

import retrosheetpy as rs

# Generate typed CREATE TABLE DDL for any dataset and database dialect
print(rs.get_ddl("events", dialect="postgres"))
print(rs.get_ddl("gamelogs", dialect="duckdb"))

docs.title: Why retrosheetpy?
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A["Retrosheet.org
(HTTP Archives)"] --> B["Smart Cache
(~/.cache/retrosheetpy)"]
    B --> C["Typed Parsers
(chadwickpy + Arrow)"]
    C --> D1["DuckDB
(Analytics)"]
    C --> D2["Parquet / Arrow
(Data Lake)"]
    C --> D3["Polars / pandas
(In-Memory)"]
    C --> D4["Postgres / Cloud
(via dlt)"]
  • Zero C Compiler Required: 100% pure Python / PyArrow wheels. Installable on Windows, macOS, and Linux in seconds with pip or uv.
  • Explicit, Strongly Typed Schemas: Dates are parsed to DATE, counts and scores to INTEGER, flags to BOOLEAN. No untyped string conversions or silent failures.
  • Smart Bandwidth Caching: Downloads once to ~/.cache/retrosheetpy/ with atomic writes, respecting Retrosheet server bandwidth.
  • Pre-Existing Table Alignment: When ingesting into existing database tables, columns are automatically mapped by name—only matching columns are inserted.
  • Complete Retrosheet Catalog: Regular season Events (play-by-play), Postseason, All-Star games, Game Logs (1871–present), Rosters, Ballparks, Schedules, Biographical encyclopedia, Ejections, and Player Transactions.

docs.title: Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)
docs.text: This document records key architectural decisions, rationales, and upstream context for retrosheetpy.

docs.title: ADR 1: Multi-Source Download Strategy (GitHub Fastly CDN as Primary)
docs.text:
• Date: 2026-10-23
  • Status: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: retrosheet.org implements strict anti-scraping policies that drop TCP SYN connections on automated bulk requests, causing persistent connection timeouts for users and automated pipelines. Upstream Retrosheet notices guide users to retrieve data via GitHub mirrors. The Chadwick Baseball Bureau maintains a public, version-controlled GitHub mirror (chadwickbureau/retrosheet) tracking upstream Retrosheet data.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Default retrosheetpy download source to the Fastly-backed GitHub raw CDN (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chadwickbureau/retrosheet/master/).
  2. Provide an "auto" mode that tries the GitHub CDN first and transparently falls back to retrosheet.org if needed.
  3. Allow users to select "github", "retrosheet", or "auto" via source parameter or --source CLI flag.
  4. Do not require personal GitHub tokens for downloading, as the raw CDN serves static files without consuming unauthenticated GitHub REST API rate limits (60 req/hr).

docs.title: ADR 2: Dynamic Season Discovery via TEAM{year} Manifest
docs.text:
• Date: 2026-10-23
  • Status: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Major League Baseball has changed team configurations, franchise locations, and league alignments repeatedly since 1871 (from 12–16 franchises in early eras to 30 modern franchises). Hardcoding team lists or attempting directory scraping causes omissions or brittle breakage across historical seasons.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: For any requested season, the downloader retrieves seasons/{year}/TEAM{year}. It parses the team codes and leagues (A for American League, N for National League), and downloads {year}{team}.EVA / {year}{team}.EVN and {team}{year}.ROS accordingly. This matches Retrosheet's native catalog format and works seamlessly with chadwickpy.roster.League.

docs.title: ADR 3: Upstream Transactions Freeze & Handover to Baseball-Reference
docs.text:
• Date: 2026-10-23
  • Status: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Retrosheet discontinued maintaining and updating its standalone transaction files (tran.txt / tranDB.zip) on November 26, 2021. Upstream responsibility for MLB transaction records was formally transitioned to Baseball-Reference.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Issue a FutureWarning when rs.transactions() is invoked, informing the user that the dataset is frozen as of November 26, 2021.
  2. Allow users to provide a local file override (~/.cache/retrosheetpy/transactions/tran.txt).
  3. For bulk ingestion and downloading pipelines (rs.download(datasets='all') or rs.to_duckdb(datasets='all')), catch unreachable remote errors for transactions and emit a warning rather than failing the entire pipeline.

docs.title: ADR 4: Promotion of polars and dlt to Core Dependencies
docs.text:
• Date: 2026-10-23
  • Status: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Baseball researchers and data engineers increasingly use modern data stacks centered on Polars, DuckDB, and dlt for direct loading into PostgreSQL, Snowflake, and BigQuery. Previously, polars and dlt were optional extras, requiring separate installation steps and causing runtime ImportError exceptions when users attempted rs.to_polars() or rs.to_dlt().

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Promote polars>=1.0.0 and dlt[duckdb,postgres,snowflake]>=1.0.0 to core dependencies in pyproject.toml. Retain pandas as an optional dependency for legacy workloads.

docs.title: ADR 5: Pydantic V2 for Configuration vs. PyArrow for Columnar Data
docs.text:
• Date: 2026-10-23
  • Status: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Retrosheet play-by-play files contain tens of millions of pitch and event records. Instantiating row-level Pydantic models introduces massive CPU overhead (100x slowdown) and memory consumption. However, structured configuration (download sources, cache parameters, connection strings) benefits significantly from Pydantic V2 validation.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Use Pydantic V2 (BaseModel) strictly for configuration models: DownloaderConfig and IngestionConfig in retrosheetpy.extract.config.
  2. Keep all tabular event and game records in columnar PyArrow Tables and RecordBatches.

docs.title: ADR 6: Zero-Copy PyArrow Streaming into dlt Resources
docs.text:
• Date: 2026-10-23
  • Status: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Previously, dlt_sink.py converted PyArrow Table batches to Python dictionaries (for batch in tbl.to_batches(): yield from batch.to_pylist()). This discarded PyArrow types (such as date32 and int16), caused memory bloat, and slowed down loading into DuckDB or PostgreSQL.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Refactor all @dlt.resource definitions in src/retrosheetpy/sink/dlt_sink.py to yield PyArrow Tables (pa.Table) directly. dlt natively consumes Arrow tables and batches with zero-copy throughput.

docs.title: ADR 7: HTTP Session Pooling and Resilient Season Extraction
docs.text:
• Date: 2026-10-23
  • Status: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: When downloading uncompressed seasons via the GitHub raw CDN, Downloader requests ~60 files per season (team manifests, individual team event files, and rosters). Recreating httpx.Client() on each request introduced connection overhead. Furthermore, raw download loops previously swallowed all exceptions indiscriminately, risking partial cache directories during network dropouts.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Lazily manage a persistent httpx.Client on Downloader with connection pooling, and implement close(), __enter__, __exit__, and __del__ for resource cleanup.
  2. In _get_events_github, distinguish expected HTTP 404s (teams with no separate event files) from network transport/timeout errors. Network errors immediately raise and clean up partial season directories to prevent cache corruption.

def allstar(
    year: int | Sequence[int],
    backend: str = "arrow",
    force: bool = False,
    downloader: Downloader | None = None,
    source: Literal["github", "retrosheet", "auto"] | None = None,
) -> Any:
    """Downloads, parses, and returns All-Star Game play-by-play events."""
    dl = _resolve_downloader(downloader=downloader, source=source)
    parser = EventParser()
    year_list = _normalize_years(year)
    tables: list[pa.Table] = []

    for y in year_list:
        extracted_dir = dl.get_allstar(y, force=force)
        files = sorted(
            list(extracted_dir.glob("*.EVA"))
            + list(extracted_dir.glob("*.EVN"))
            + list(extracted_dir.glob("*.EVE"))

    else:
        consolidated = pa.concat_tables(tables)

    return _convert_backend(consolidated, backend)

def download(
    years: int | Sequence[int] | None = None,
    datasets: Sequence[str] | str = "all",
    force: bool = False,
    downloader: Downloader | None = None,
    source: Literal["github", "retrosheet", "auto"] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, list[Path]]:
    """Downloads specified Retrosheet archives to local cache without loading them into memory.

    Args:
        years: Year or sequence of years to download. Defaults to [2024] if not provided.
        datasets: Dataset or comma-separated list of datasets to download
            ('events', 'postseason', 'allstar', 'gamelogs', 'rosters', 'parks',
             'schedules', 'bio', 'ejections', 'transactions', or 'all').
        force: If True, re-downloads even if already cached.
        downloader: Optional custom Downloader instance.
        source: Optional source override ('github', 'retrosheet', or 'auto').

    Returns:
        Dictionary mapping dataset name to list of extracted paths or file locations.
    """
    dl = _resolve_downloader(downloader=downloader, source=source)
    results: dict[str, list[Path]] = {}

    all_supported = [
        "events",
        "postseason",
        "allstar",
        "gamelogs",
        "rosters",
        "parks",
        "schedules",
        "bio",
        "ejections",
        "transactions",
    ]

    if isinstance(datasets, str):
        if datasets.lower() == "all":
            selected = all_supported
        else:
            selected = [d.strip().lower() for d in datasets.split(",") if d.strip()]
    else:
        selected = [d.lower() for d in datasets]

    year_list = _normalize_years(years) if years is not None else [2024]

    for d in selected:
        results[d] = []
        if d == "events":
            for y in year_list:
                p = dl.get_events(y, force=force)
                results[d].append(p)
        elif d == "postseason":
            for y in year_list:
                p = dl.get_postseason(y, force=force)
                results[d].append(p)
        elif d == "allstar":
            for y in year_list:
                p = dl.get_allstar(y, force=force)
                results[d].append(p)
        elif d in ("gamelogs", "game_logs"):
            for y in year_list:
                p = dl.get_gamelogs(y, force=force)
                results[d].append(p)
        elif d == "rosters":
            for y in year_list:
                p = dl.get_events(y, force=force)
                results[d].append(p)
        elif d == "schedules":
            for y in year_list:
                p = dl.get_schedules(y, force=force)
                results[d].append(p)
        elif d == "parks":
            p = dl.get_parks(force=force)
            results[d].append(p)
        elif d == "bio":
            p = dl.get_bio(force=force)
            results[d].append(p)
        elif d == "ejections":
            p = dl.get_ejections(force=force)
            results[d].append(p)
        elif d == "transactions":
            try:
                p = dl.get_transactions(force=force)
                results[d].append(p)
            except FileNotFoundError as err:
                warnings.warn(
                    f"Skipping transactions download: {err}",
                    UserWarning,
                    stacklevel=2,
                )

    return results

def to_dlt(

    years: int | Sequence[int] = 2024,
    datasets: Sequence[str] = ("events", "gamelogs", "rosters", "parks"),
    pipeline_name: str = "retrosheet",
    downloader: Downloader | None = None,
    source: Literal["github", "retrosheet", "auto"] | None = None,
    **dlt_kwargs: Any,
) -> Any:
    """Runs a full dlt pipeline ingesting Retrosheet datasets into Postgres, Snowflake, DuckDB, etc."""
    try:
        import dlt
    except ImportError as err:
        raise ImportError("dlt is not installed. Install it via 'pip install dlt'.") from err

def to_duckdb(
    path: Path | str,

    datasets: Sequence[str] = ("events", "gamelogs", "rosters", "parks"),
    force: bool = False,
    downloader: Downloader | None = None,
    source: Literal["github", "retrosheet", "auto"] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Ingests selected Retrosheet datasets into a DuckDB database."""
    dl = _resolve_downloader(downloader=downloader, source=source)
    sink = DuckDBSink(db_path=path)

    try:
        ds_set = set(d.lower() for d in datasets)

        if "parks" in ds_set:
            tbl_parks = parks(backend="arrow", force=force, downloader=dl)
            sink.write_table("parks", tbl_parks)

        if "bio" in ds_set:

        if "ejections" in ds_set:
            tbl_ej = ejections(backend="arrow", force=force, downloader=dl)

        if "transactions" in ds_set:
            try:

            sink.write_table("schedules", tbl_sked)

        if "gamelogs" in ds_set or "game_logs" in ds_set:
            tbl_gl = game_logs(year=years, backend="arrow", force=force, downloader=dl)
            sink.write_table("game_logs", tbl_gl)

        if "rosters" in ds_set:
            tbl_rosters = rosters(year=years, backend="arrow", force=force, downloader=dl)
            sink.write_table("rosters", tbl_rosters)

        if "events" in ds_set:
            tbl_events = events(year=years, backend="arrow", force=force, downloader=dl)

        if "postseason" in ds_set:

docs.title: retrosheetpy download

Downloads and caches specified Retrosheet archives locally without loading them into memory or writing to an external database:

retrosheetpy download [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Recipe: Ballpark Factors & Scoring Environments
docs.text:
A Park Factor (PF) measures how much a specific ballpark inflates or deflates run scoring compared to an average stadium.

A park factor of 100 is neutral. Values above 100 (e.g. 115 at Coors Field) indicate hitter-friendly parks, while values below 100 (e.g. 88 at Petco Park) indicate pitcher-friendly environments.

docs.title: The Formula
docs.text:
The standard basic 1-year Run Park Factor is:

$$\text{PF} = \frac{\frac{\text{Runs at Home}}{\text{Games at Home}}}{\frac{\text{Runs on Road}}{\text{Games on Road}}} \times 100$$

docs.title: Calculating Park Factors with DuckDB
docs.text:
import retrosheetpy as rs
import duckdb

# Ingest 2024 game logs and parks into DuckDB
rs.to_duckdb("retro.duckdb", years=[2024], datasets=["gamelogs", "parks"])

con = duckdb.connect("retro.duckdb")

query = """
WITH home_runs_scored AS (
    SELECT
        home_team AS team,
        park_id,
        COUNT(*) AS home_games,
        SUM(home_score + visiting_score) AS home_runs
    FROM game_logs
    GROUP BY home_team, park_id
),
road_runs_scored AS (
    SELECT
        visiting_team AS team,
        COUNT(*) AS road_games,
        SUM(home_score + visiting_score) AS road_runs
    FROM game_logs
    GROUP BY visiting_team
)
SELECT
    p.name AS ballpark,
    h.team,
    h.home_games,
    h.home_runs,
    r.road_runs,
    ROUND(((h.home_runs / h.home_games) / (r.road_runs / r.road_games)) * 100, 1) AS park_factor
FROM home_runs_scored h
JOIN road_runs_scored r ON h.team = r.team
JOIN parks p ON h.park_id = p.park_id
ORDER BY park_factor DESC;
"""

pf_df = con.execute(query).fetchdf()
print(pf_df.head(10))

docs.title: Recipe: Platoon Splits (Batter vs. Pitcher Handedness)
docs.text:
The platoon advantage is one of the most fundamental dynamics in baseball: batters almost universally hit better against opposite-handed pitchers (Left vs. Right or Right vs. Left) because the ball breaks toward their vision plane.

retrosheetpy event files include both BAT_HAND_CD (L, R, S) and PIT_HAND_CD (L, R) on every single play.

docs.title: Computing Platoon Splits in Polars
docs.text:
import retrosheetpy as rs
import polars as pl

# 1. Download 2024 play-by-play events
events = rs.events(year=2024, backend="polars")

# 2. Filter for official at-bats
ab_events = events.filter(pl.col("AB_FL") == True)

# 3. Calculate Batting Average and Slugging by Matchup Handedness
splits = (
    ab_events.group_by(["BAT_HAND_CD", "PIT_HAND_CD"])
    .agg(
        [
            pl.len().alias("at_bats"),
            pl.col("H_FL").cast(pl.Int32).sum().alias("hits"),
            pl.col("HR_FL").cast(pl.Int32).sum().alias("home_runs"),
        ]
    )
    .with_columns(
        [
            (pl.col("hits") / pl.col("at_bats")).round(3).alias("batting_avg"),
            (pl.col("home_runs") / pl.col("at_bats")).round(4).alias("hr_rate"),
        ]
    )
    .sort(["BAT_HAND_CD", "PIT_HAND_CD"])
)

print(splits)

docs.title: Recipe: Production Pipelines & Orchestration
docs.text:
For data engineers and analytics teams maintaining a production data warehouse (PostgreSQL, Snowflake, BigQuery, or MotherDuck), Retrosheet ingestion should run as an automated, idempotent ELT pipeline.

This guide outlines an end-to-end production pipeline pattern using retrosheetpy, SQL DDL, and dlt.

docs.title: Pattern: Schema Setup -> Staging -> Load
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Pipeline as Orchestrator (Airflow / Cron)
    participant RS as retrosheetpy
    participant DB as Production Database

    Pipeline->>RS: rs.get_ddl("gamelogs", dialect="postgres")
    RS-->>Pipeline: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ...
    Pipeline->>DB: Execute DDL (Idempotent table creation)
    Pipeline->>RS: rs.to_dlt(destination, years=[2024], ...)
    RS->>DB: Stream typed Arrow RecordBatches (0.1s load)

docs.title: Production Python Script (sync_retrosheet.py)
docs.text:
import os
import dlt
import retrosheetpy as rs
from sqlalchemy import create_engine, text

# 1. Connection string from environment variable
DB_URI = os.getenv("DATABASE_URL", "postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/retrosheet")

# 2. Pre-create strongly-typed tables using DDL generator
engine = create_engine(DB_URI)
with engine.begin() as conn:
    for dataset in ["gamelogs", "rosters", "parks"]:
        ddl = rs.get_ddl(dataset, dialect="postgres")
        conn.execute(text(ddl))

# 3. Stream data via dlt
pipeline = dlt.pipeline(
    pipeline_name="retrosheet_production_sync",
    destination=dlt.destinations.postgres(DB_URI),
    dataset_name="public",
)

# Ingest current season with replace disposition
source = rs.to_dlt(
    destination=dlt.destinations.postgres(DB_URI),
    years=[2024],
    datasets=["gamelogs", "rosters", "parks"],
    dataset_name="public",
)

print("Pipeline synchronization complete!")

docs.title: Recipe: 24-State Run Expectancy (RE24)
docs.text:
In sabermetrics, the Run Expectancy Matrix (RE24) calculates the average number of runs scored from any given game state (combination of 0, 1, or 2 outs and runners on 1st, 2nd, and 3rd) through the end of that half-inning.

This tutorial shows how to construct the official RE24 matrix using 2024 Retrosheet events in DuckDB.

docs.title: 1. Ingest 2024 Events into DuckDB
docs.text:
import retrosheetpy as rs

# Download and load 2024 play-by-play events
rs.to_duckdb("retro.duckdb", years=[2024], datasets=["events"])

docs.title: 2. Compute Run Expectancy via SQL
docs.text:
Each play record in Retrosheet includes: * GAME_ID: Unique game * INN_CT: Inning * BAT_HOME_ID: Half-inning (0 = top, 1 = bottom) * OUTS_CT: Outs before play (0, 1, 2) * BASE1_RUN_ID, BASE2_RUN_ID, BASE3_RUN_ID: Base runners * AWAY_SCORE_CT, HOME_SCORE_CT: Current score

import duckdb

con = duckdb.connect("retro.duckdb")

query = """
WITH half_innings AS (
    -- Total runs scored in each half-inning
    SELECT
        GAME_ID,
        INN_CT,
        BAT_HOME_ID,
        MAX(CASE WHEN BAT_HOME_ID = 0 THEN AWAY_SCORE_CT ELSE HOME_SCORE_CT END) -
        MIN(CASE WHEN BAT_HOME_ID = 0 THEN AWAY_SCORE_CT ELSE HOME_SCORE_CT END) AS runs_in_half_inning
    FROM events
    GROUP BY GAME_ID, INN_CT, BAT_HOME_ID
),
play_states AS (
    -- Base runners state encoded as string: '---', '1--', '-2-', '12-', '123', etc.
    SELECT
        e.GAME_ID,
        e.INN_CT,
        e.BAT_HOME_ID,
        e.OUTS_CT,
        CONCAT(
            CASE WHEN e.BASE1_RUN_ID IS NOT NULL AND e.BASE1_RUN_ID != '' THEN '1' ELSE '-' END,
            CASE WHEN e.BASE2_RUN_ID IS NOT NULL AND e.BASE2_RUN_ID != '' THEN '2' ELSE '-' END,
            CASE WHEN e.BASE3_RUN_ID IS NOT NULL AND e.BASE3_RUN_ID != '' THEN '3' ELSE '-' END
        ) AS base_state,
        -- Runs scored from this point forward until 3 outs
        h.runs_in_half_inning - (CASE WHEN e.BAT_HOME_ID = 0 THEN e.AWAY_SCORE_CT ELSE e.HOME_SCORE_CT END) AS future_runs
    FROM events e
    JOIN half_innings h
      ON e.GAME_ID = h.GAME_ID
     AND e.INN_CT = h.INN_CT
     AND e.BAT_HOME_ID = h.BAT_HOME_ID
)
SELECT
    base_state,
    ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN OUTS_CT = 0 THEN future_runs END), 3) AS "0 Outs",
    ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN OUTS_CT = 1 THEN future_runs END), 3) AS "1 Out",
    ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN OUTS_CT = 2 THEN future_runs END), 3) AS "2 Outs",
    COUNT(*) AS total_plays
FROM play_states
GROUP BY base_state
ORDER BY "0 Outs" DESC;
"""

re24_table = con.execute(query).fetchdf()
print(re24_table)

docs.title: Official Ejections Log
docs.text:
Retrosheet's official ejections database records every known ejection in Major League Baseball history (1889–present).

Each ejection entry records the game ID, date, double header flag, ejectee (player, manager, coach, trainer), ejecting umpire, inning, and the official rationale.

docs.title: Python API Usage
docs.text:
import retrosheetpy as rs

# 1. Fetch ejections log into Polars
ej_df = rs.ejections(backend="polars")

# Top reasons for ejection
print(ej_df.group_by("reason").count().sort("count", descending=True).head(10))

# 2. Ingest into DuckDB
rs.to_duckdb("baseball.duckdb", datasets=["ejections"])

# 3. Export to Parquet
rs.to_parquet("ejections.parquet", dataset="ejections")

docs.title: CLI Usage
docs.text:
# Download and cache ejections log
retrosheetpy download -s ejections

# Export to Parquet
retrosheetpy export -s ejections -f parquet -o ejections.parquet

# Generate Postgres DDL
retrosheetpy ddl -s ejections --dialect postgres

docs.title: PyArrow Schema (EJECTION_SCHEMA)
docs.text: Column Name Arrow Type SQL Dialects Description game_id pa.string() VARCHAR / STRING Retrosheet Game ID (e.g. BOS202404010). date pa.date32() DATE Date of the game (YYYY-MM-DD). dh pa.string() VARCHAR / STRING Doubleheader game index if applicable. ejectee_id pa.string() VARCHAR / STRING Player or personnel Retrosheet ID. ejectee_name pa.string() VARCHAR / STRING Full name of the ejected individual. team_id pa.string() VARCHAR / STRING Three-letter team abbreviation. job pa.string() VARCHAR / STRING Role code (P player, M manager, C coach, etc.). umpire_id pa.string() VARCHAR / STRING Retrosheet ID of the ejecting umpire. umpire_name pa.string() VARCHAR / STRING Name of the ejecting umpire. inning pa.int8() SMALLINT / INT64 Inning in which the ejection occurred. reason pa.string() VARCHAR / STRING Documented reason (e.g. Balls and strikes, Arguments).

docs.title: Play-by-Play Events
docs.text:
Retrosheet event files (.EVA, .EVN) record every pitch, play, substitution, and baserunning event in Major League Baseball.

retrosheetpy parses these event archives into a 164-column strongly-typed schema via chadwickpy.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
import retrosheetpy as rs

# Download & parse 2024 plays (returns Polars DataFrame)
events = rs.events(year=2024, backend="polars")

# Filter for home runs
home_runs = events.filter(events["HR_FL"] == True)
print(f"Total 2024 MLB Home Runs: {home_runs.height}")

docs.title: Key Column Reference (164 Columns)
docs.text: The full 164 columns are categorized below:

docs.title: 1. Game & State Identifiers
docs.text: Column Type Description GAME_ID string Retrosheet game identifier (e.g. BOS202404090) YEAR int32 Season year (e.g. 2024) INN_CT int16 Inning number (1–9+) BAT_HOME_ID int16 Batting team flag (0 = Visiting, 1 = Home) OUTS_CT int16 Outs before play occurred (0, 1, 2) BALLS_CT int16 Balls before play occurred (0–3) STRIKES_CT int16 Strikes before play occurred (0–2) PITCH_SEQ_TX string Pitches thrown in the plate appearance (e.g. BBSFX)

docs.title: 2. Player Identifiers
docs.text: Column Type Description BAT_ID string Retrosheet player ID of batter (e.g. ohtas001) BAT_HAND_CD string Batter handedness (L, R, S) RESP_BAT_ID string Batter responsible for the plate appearance PIT_ID string Pitcher ID PIT_HAND_CD string Pitcher handedness (L, R) RESP_PIT_ID string Pitcher responsible for runners / run POS2_FLD_ID - POS9_FLD_ID string Player IDs for fielders by position (Catcher through RF)

docs.title: 3. Base Runners
docs.text: Column Type Description BASE1_RUN_ID string Runner on first before play (empty if vacant) BASE2_RUN_ID string Runner on second before play BASE3_RUN_ID string Runner on third before play

docs.title: 4. Play Details & Scores
docs.text: Column Type Description EVENT_TX string Raw Retrosheet play descriptor (e.g. HR/7/F, K, S8/L.1-3) EVENT_CD int16 Chadwick numeric event code (e.g. 23 = Home run) AWAY_SCORE_CT int16 Visiting team score before play HOME_SCORE_CT int16 Home team score before play RBI_CT int16 Runs batted in on play EVENT_OUTS_CT int16 Number of outs recorded on play (0, 1, 2, 3)

docs.title: 5. Boolean Indicators
docs.text: Column Type Description AB_FL bool At-bat indicator H_FL bool Hit indicator (single, double, triple, HR) SH_FL bool Sacrifice hit / bunt SF_FL bool Sacrifice fly DP_FL bool Double play turned on play TP_FL bool Triple play turned on play HR_FL bool Home run hit on play WP_FL bool Wild pitch occurred PB_FL bool Passed ball occurred

docs.title: Multi-Season Processing
docs.text:
You can fetch multiple seasons in a single call. retrosheetpy automatically concatenates the Arrow record batches efficiently:

import retrosheetpy as rs

# 2020 through 2024 (approx 900,000 plays)
multi_events = rs.events(year=range(2020, 2025), backend="polars")

docs.title: Historical Game Logs
docs.text:
Retrosheet's historical game logs cover every official Major League Baseball game from 1871 to the present day (over 230,000 games).

Each game log contains 161 columns recording game date, participating teams, final scores, line scores, team statistics, umpire crews, winning/losing pitchers, and starting lineups.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
import retrosheetpy as rs

# Download and parse 2024 game logs
gl = rs.game_logs(year=2024, backend="polars")

# Look at opening day games
opening_day = gl.filter(gl["date"] == "2024-03-28").select(
    ["visiting_team", "visiting_score", "home_team", "home_score", "attendance"]
)
print(opening_day)

docs.title: Schema Overview (161 Columns)
docs.text: The game log schema uses strict native types rather than strings:

docs.title: 1. General Game Metadata
docs.text: Column Type Example Description date date32 2024-03-28 Official game date game_number int16 0, 1, 2 Doubleheader indicator (0 = single game) day_of_week string Thu Day of week visiting_team string LAN Visiting team 3-letter code visiting_league string NL Visiting team league (AL, NL) visiting_game_num int16 1 Game number for visiting team in season home_team string SDN Home team 3-letter code home_league string NL Home team league home_game_num int16 1 Game number for home team in season visiting_score int16 5 Runs scored by visitor home_score int16 2 Runs scored by home team outs_total int16 54 Length of game in outs (54 = standard 9 innings) day_night string D, N Day or night game indicator park_id string SEO01 Retrosheet ballpark ID attendance int32 15952 Paid attendance (nullable) game_time_minutes int16 185 Length of game in minutes

docs.title: 2. Line Scores
docs.text: Column Type Description visiting_linescore string Inning-by-inning runs for visitor (e.g. 000101003) home_linescore string Inning-by-inning runs for home team (e.g. 000000020)

docs.title: 3. Team Statistics (Both Visiting & Home)
docs.text: Columns are prefixed with v_ (visiting) and h_ (home): * at_bats, hits, doubles, triples, home_runs, rbi (int16) * walks, intentional_walks, strikeouts, stolen_bases, caught_stealing (int16) * errors, passed_balls, double_plays, triple_plays (int16) * pitchers_used, individual_earned_runs, team_earned_runs (int16)

docs.title: 4. Personnel & Pitchers of Record
docs.text: Column Type Description winning_pitcher_id / name string Winning pitcher ID & full name losing_pitcher_id / name string Losing pitcher ID & full name saving_pitcher_id / name string Saving pitcher ID & full name (if applicable) visiting_manager_id / name string Visiting team manager home_manager_id / name string Home team manager hp_umpire_id / name string Home plate umpire

docs.title: 5. Starting Lineups
docs.text: For positions 1 through 9 for both visitor (v_batter_1_id ... v_batter_9_id) and home (h_batter_1_id ... h_batter_9_id), including fielding position code (1–10, where 10 = DH).

docs.title: Ballpark Directory
docs.text: The Retrosheet ballpark directory (parkcode.txt) catalogs every historical Major League Baseball ballpark, stadium, and neutral site since 1871.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
import retrosheetpy as rs

# Download and parse ballpark encyclopedia
parks = rs.parks(backend="polars")

# Look at ballparks in New York
ny_parks = parks.filter(parks["state"] == "NY")
print(ny_parks.select(["park_id", "name", "city", "start_date", "end_date"]))

docs.title: Schema Reference
docs.text: Column Type Example Description park_id string BOS07 Retrosheet unique 5-character park code name string Fenway Park Official ballpark name aka string Fenway Park Alternative name / historical moniker city string Boston City location state string MA 2-letter state code start_date date32 1912-04-20 First major league game date end_date date32 null Last major league game date (null if active) league string AL Primary league notes string ... Historical notes, demolition details, etc.

docs.title: Joining Ballparks with Game Logs
docs.text:
You can join the ballpark directory with historical game logs to inspect runs scored by stadium:

import retrosheetpy as rs

# Load 2024 game logs and parks
gl = rs.game_logs(year=2024, backend="polars")
parks = rs.parks(backend="polars")

# Join on park_id
games_with_park = gl.join(parks, on="park_id", how="left")
print(games_with_park.select(["date", "name", "visiting_team", "home_team", "attendance"]).head(10))

docs.title: Postseason & All-Star Games
docs.text:
In addition to regular season play-by-play archives, Retrosheet distributes dedicated event files for Postseason series (World Series, LCS, LDS, Wild Card) and the annual All-Star Game.

retrosheetpy parses these specialty archives directly through the standard 164-column Chadwick event schema contract.

docs.title: Python API Usage
docs.text:
import retrosheetpy as rs

# 1. Fetch 2024 Postseason events into Polars
post_df = rs.postseason(2024, backend="polars")
print(f"Total Postseason plays: {len(post_df)}")

# 2. Fetch 2024 All-Star Game events into Polars
as_df = rs.allstar(2024, backend="polars")

# 3. Export Postseason events to Parquet
rs.to_parquet("postseason_2024.parquet", dataset="postseason", years=2024)

# 4. Ingest Postseason & All-Star into DuckDB
rs.to_duckdb(
    "october.duckdb",
    years=[2021, 2022, 2023, 2024],
    datasets=["postseason", "allstar"],
)

docs.title: CLI Usage
docs.text:
# Download and cache Postseason & All-Star archives
retrosheetpy download -s postseason,allstar -y 2024

# Export 2024 Postseason to Parquet
retrosheetpy export -s postseason -y 2024 -f parquet -o postseason_2024.parquet

# Export 2024 All-Star Game to CSV
retrosheetpy export -s allstar -y 2024 -f csv -o allstar_2024.csv

# Ingest into local DuckDB
retrosheetpy ingest -d duckdb -c fall_classic.duckdb -s postseason -y 2020-2024

docs.title: Schema Contract
docs.text:
Both postseason and allstar events conform directly to EVENT_SCHEMA (164 fields), providing pitch sequences, hit coordinates, base runner advances, pickoff attempts, and run expectancy states identical to regular season events.

For complete field definitions and physical data types, see the Play-by-Play Events Reference.

docs.title: Team Rosters
docs.text: Retrosheet roster files (.ROS) record official rosters for every team in a given season, linking player IDs with full names, batting handedness, throwing handedness, and primary positions.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
import retrosheetpy as rs

# Download & parse 2024 MLB rosters
rosters = rs.rosters(year=2024, backend="polars")

# Look at Los Angeles Dodgers roster
dodgers = rosters.filter(rosters["team"] == "LAN")
print(dodgers.select(["player_id", "first_name", "last_name", "bats", "throws", "position"]))

docs.title: Schema Reference
docs.text: Column Type Example Description player_id string ohtas001 Unique 8-character Retrosheet player ID last_name string Ohtani Player surname first_name string Shohei Player given name bats string L, R, B Batting handedness (L = Left, R = Right, B = Both/Switch) throws string R, L Throwing handedness (R = Right, L = Left) team string LAN Team code for this season position string DH, P, SS Primary fielding position year int32 2024 Season year

docs.title: Multi-Year Roster Tracking
docs.text:
You can track a player's team changes across multiple seasons:

import retrosheetpy as rs

# Fetch rosters from 2018 to 2024
multi_ros = rs.rosters(year=range(2018, 2025), backend="polars")

# Filter for a specific player
shohei_career = multi_ros.filter(multi_ros["player_id"] == "ohtas001")
print(shohei_career.select(["year", "team", "position"]))

docs.title: Official Schedules
docs.text:
Retrosheet publishes regular season schedule files for every season in Major League Baseball history (1877–present).

Each season's archive (YYYYSKED.zip) contains the game date, doubleheader number, opponent matchups, leagues, day/night flag, venue, postponed status, and makeup date.

docs.title: Python API Usage
docs.text:
import retrosheetpy as rs

# 1. Fetch 2024 schedule into Polars
sked_df = rs.schedules(2024, backend="polars")
print(sked_df.select(["date", "vis_team", "home_team", "day_night", "postponed"]))

# 2. Fetch multi-year schedules into PyArrow Table
sked_tbl = rs.schedules(range(2020, 2025), backend="arrow")

# 3. Export to Parquet
rs.to_parquet("schedules_2024.parquet", dataset="schedules", years=2024)

docs.title: CLI Usage
docs.text:
# Download and cache schedule files
retrosheetpy download -s schedules -y 2024

# Export to Parquet
retrosheetpy export -s schedules -y 2024 -f parquet -o schedules_2024.parquet

# Generate BigQuery SQL DDL
retrosheetpy ddl -s schedules --dialect bigquery

# Ingest into DuckDB
retrosheetpy ingest -d duckdb -c baseball.duckdb -s schedules -y 2024

docs.title: PyArrow Schema (SCHEDULE_SCHEMA)
docs.text: Column Name Arrow Type SQL (Postgres / BigQuery) Description date pa.date32() DATE Scheduled game date (YYYY-MM-DD). game_num pa.int8() SMALLINT / INT64 0 for single game, 1/2 for doubleheaders. day_of_week pa.string() VARCHAR / STRING Three-letter or full day of week (Mon, Tue, etc.). vis_team pa.string() VARCHAR / STRING Visiting team three-letter abbreviation (e.g. LAN). vis_league pa.string() VARCHAR / STRING Visiting team league (AL, NL, AA, etc.). vis_game_num pa.int16() SMALLINT / INT64 Visiting team's game number in season. home_team pa.string() VARCHAR / STRING Home team three-letter abbreviation (e.g. SDN). home_league pa.string() VARCHAR / STRING Home team league (AL, NL, etc.). home_game_num pa.int16() SMALLINT / INT64 Home team's game number in season. day_night pa.string() VARCHAR / STRING D for Day game, N for Night game. park_id pa.string() VARCHAR / STRING Neutral site or special ballpark ID if applicable. postponed pa.string() VARCHAR / STRING Postponement reason (e.g. Rain, Cold, Strike) or empty. makeup_date pa.date32() DATE Rescheduled makeup date if postponed.

docs.title: Player Transactions Database
docs.text:
Retrosheet's transactions database (tranDB.zip containing tran.txt) tracks player trades, free agent signings, waivers, releases, purchases, and draft picks spanning baseball history.

Each transaction record captures dates, chronological ordering, transaction type codes, trading clubs, draft round, pick numbers, and supplemental terms.

docs.title: Python API Usage
docs.text:
import retrosheetpy as rs

# 1. Fetch transactions into Polars
tran_df = rs.transactions(backend="polars")

# Trades involving a specific player
ohtani_moves = tran_df.filter(tran_df["player_id"] == "ohtas001")
print(ohtani_moves.select(["primary_date", "type", "from_team", "to_team", "info"]))

# 2. Ingest into DuckDB
rs.to_duckdb("baseball.duckdb", datasets=["transactions"])

# 3. Export to Parquet
rs.to_parquet("transactions.parquet", dataset="transactions")

docs.title: CLI Usage
docs.text:
# Download and cache transactions archive
retrosheetpy download -s transactions

# Export to Parquet
retrosheetpy export -s transactions -f parquet -o transactions.parquet

# Generate DDL
retrosheetpy ddl -s transactions --dialect postgres

docs.title: PyArrow Schema (TRANSACTION_SCHEMA)
docs.text: Column Name Arrow Type SQL Dialects Description primary_date pa.date32() DATE Effective transaction date (YYYY-MM-DD). time pa.string() VARCHAR / STRING Chronological ordering flag (1 between games, 2 after games). approx_indicator pa.string() VARCHAR / STRING @ if primary date is approximate. secondary_date pa.date32() DATE Associated secondary date (e.g. trade completion date). approx_indicator_sec pa.string() VARCHAR / STRING @ if secondary date is approximate. transaction_id pa.string() VARCHAR / STRING Unique transaction record identifier. player_id pa.string() VARCHAR / STRING Retrosheet player identifier. type pa.string() VARCHAR / STRING Transaction type code (T trade, F free agent, D draft, etc.). from_team pa.string() VARCHAR / STRING Relinquishing team abbreviation. from_league pa.string() VARCHAR / STRING Relinquishing league. to_team pa.string() VARCHAR / STRING Acquiring team abbreviation. to_league pa.string() VARCHAR / STRING Acquiring league. draft_type pa.string() VARCHAR / STRING Amateur, rule 5, or expansion draft code. draft_round pa.int16() SMALLINT / INT64 Draft round number. pick_number pa.int16() SMALLINT / INT64 Overall draft pick number. info pa.string() VARCHAR / STRING Supplemental trade notes and conditions.

docs.title: Architecture & Design Philosophy
docs.text: retrosheetpy is engineered around four core tenets: zero compiler requirements, strict schema typing, pipeline decoupling, and respect for Retrosheet server resources.

docs.title: Decoupled Pipeline Architecture
docs.text:
Each stage of the data pipeline is isolated in its own package with clean contracts:

flowchart TD
    subgraph Extract ["1. extract/ (Network & Cache)"]
        Manifest["Manifest URL Registry"]
        Downloader["Resilient Downloader (httpx)"]
        Cache["Atomic Cache Manager (~/.cache/retrosheetpy)"]
    end

    subgraph Parse ["2. parse/ & schemas/ (Type Enforcement)"]
        EventParser["EventParser (chadwickpy Bridge)"]
        GLParser["GameLogParser"]
        RosterParser["RosterParser"]
        ParkParser["ParkParser"]
        Schemas["Explicit PyArrow Schemas (164/161 Columns)"]
    end

    subgraph Sink ["3. sink/ (Multi-Destination Output)"]
        DuckDBSink["DuckDBSink (Embedded Analytics)"]
        FileSink["FileSink (Parquet / Arrow / CSV)"]
        DFSink["DataframeConverter (Polars, pandas)"]
        DLTSink["DLTSink (@dlt.source Generator)"]
    end

    Extract --> Parse --> Sink

docs.title: 1. extract/ (Network & Caching)
docs.text:
• manifest.py: Resolves canonical Retrosheet HTTP endpoints (e.g. https://www.retrosheet.org/events/2024eve.zip, with automated fallback to {year}seve.zip for older archive conventions).
  • cache.py: Manages atomic downloads, extracted archive trees, and cache eviction under ~/.cache/retrosheetpy/ (configurable via RETROSHEETPY_CACHE_DIR).
  • downloader.py: Handles retries, HTTP status verification, and decompression safely.

docs.title: 2. schemas/ & parse/ (Strict Typing)
docs.text:
• No VARCHAR-only Dumps: In many tools, raw files are loaded with everything as strings. retrosheetpy provides strict schemas:
  • Game dates are parsed to date32().
  • Outs, innings, balls, strikes, and base states are parsed to int16() or int32().
  • Flags (HR_FL, RBI_FL, SH_FL, SF_FL, etc.) are parsed to bool_().
  • Chadwick Integration: Uses pure Python chadwickpy wheels to process Retrosheet event files without subprocesses or C tool binaries.

docs.title: 3. sink/ (Pluggable Output Writers)
docs.text:
• The parsers emit standard PyArrow Tables or record iterators.
  • Sinks write directly into:
  • DuckDB: Fast in-memory or persisted SQL engine with automatic column alignment.
  • Parquet / Arrow: Snappy-compressed columnar formats.
  • Polars & pandas: In-memory DataFrames for data science.
  • dlt: Modern pipeline framework targeting PostgreSQL, Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, etc.

docs.title: Pre-Existing Table Alignment
docs.text:
A major problem for DBAs loading Retrosheet into existing production databases is schema mismatches: an existing table might have columns in a different order or contain additional metadata columns.

retrosheetpy automatically queries the destination table's schema, matches columns by name between the incoming Retrosheet data and the target table, and generates an aligned INSERT INTO target (matching_cols) SELECT ... statement.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: retrosheetpy is available on PyPI and requires Python 3.11 or higher. It is packaged with pre-compiled wheels for Windows, macOS, and Linux, meaning no C compiler or build tools are required.

docs.title: Basic Installation
docs.text:
Install the base package with pip or uv:

uv (Recommended)pip 
uv add retrosheetpy

pip install retrosheetpy

docs.text:
retrosheetpy is designed to be lean by default. You can install optional dependencies depending on your workflow:

After installation, verify that the CLI and Python package are functional:

retrosheetpy --version

Or from Python:

print(rs.__version__)

docs.title: 5-Minute Quickstart
docs.text: This guide walks through downloading Retrosheet data, querying play-by-play events, and saving datasets to DuckDB and Parquet.

docs.title: 1. Downloading & Inspecting Events
docs.text:
To fetch every play of the 2024 MLB season (all ~188,000 plays across 2,429 games):

import retrosheetpy as rs

# Download, cache, and parse 2024 play-by-play
events = rs.events(year=2024, backend="polars")

# Inspect plays
print(events.select(["GAME_ID", "INN_CT", "BAT_ID", "PIT_ID", "EVENT_TX"]).head(10))

The returned table contains 164 strongly-typed columns, including count, pitch sequence, base runners, event codes, and defensive alignment.

docs.title: 2. Historical Game Logs (1871–Present)
docs.text:
Retrosheet provides game-by-game summary logs with line scores, starting lineups, umpire crews, and attendance.

import retrosheetpy as rs

# Fetch multiple seasons at once
gl = rs.game_logs(year=[2023, 2024], backend="polars")

# Find the highest scoring games of 2024
high_scoring = gl.filter(gl["visiting_score"] + gl["home_score"] > 20).select(
    ["date", "visiting_team", "visiting_score", "home_team", "home_score"]
)
print(high_scoring)

docs.title: 3. Ballparks & Rosters
docs.text:
Explore the historical ballpark encyclopedia and official team rosters:

import retrosheetpy as rs

# 1. Complete ballpark directory (260 historical major league parks)
parks = rs.parks(backend="polars")
print(parks.filter(parks["city"] == "Chicago"))

# 2. 2024 Player rosters
rosters = rs.rosters(year=2024, backend="polars")
shohei = rosters.filter(rosters["last_name"] == "Ohtani")
print(shohei)

docs.title: 4. Ingesting into DuckDB
docs.text:
Instead of storing gigabytes of raw CSV or text files, you can stream multiple seasons and datasets directly into an embedded DuckDB file:

import retrosheetpy as rs

# Ingest full 2020-2024 seasons into local DuckDB
rs.to_duckdb(
    path="retro.duckdb",
    years=range(2020, 2025),
    datasets=["events", "gamelogs", "rosters", "parks"],
)

Now connect to DuckDB directly with SQL:

import duckdb

con = duckdb.connect("retro.duckdb")

# Top home run hitters of 2024
top_hr = con.execute("""
    SELECT BAT_ID, COUNT(*) AS home_runs
    FROM events
    WHERE HR_FL = TRUE AND YEAR = 2024
    GROUP BY BAT_ID
    ORDER BY home_runs DESC
    LIMIT 10
""").fetchdf()

print(top_hr)

docs.title: 5. Exporting to Parquet
docs.text:
For fast columnar storage in S3 or local data lakes:

import retrosheetpy as rs

rs.to_parquet(
    path="gamelogs_2000_2024.parquet",
    dataset="gamelogs",
    years=range(2000, 2025),
)

docs.title: Cloud Warehouses via dlt
docs.text:
dlt (Data Load Tool) is an open-source library that automates schema extraction, typing, and resilient data loading into enterprise data warehouses and relational databases.

retrosheetpy exposes a dedicated @dlt.source generator and the top-level helper rs.to_dlt() to stream Retrosheet datasets directly into PostgreSQL, Snowflake, Google BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift, and DuckDB.

docs.title: Out-of-the-Box Ingestion
docs.text:
dlt is included directly in retrosheetpy's core dependencies. retrosheetpy's dlt sources yield native PyArrow Tables (pyarrow.Table) directly into dlt without converting rows to Python dictionaries, ensuring zero-copy throughput and strict type preservation into destination databases.

pip install retrosheetpy

docs.title: Direct Pipeline Execution (to_dlt)
docs.text:
To load multiple seasons directly into a database with a single call:

import retrosheetpy as rs

# Stream 2023-2024 rosters, ballparks, and game logs into PostgreSQL
info = rs.to_dlt(
    destination="postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/retrosheet",
    years=[2023, 2024],
    datasets=["rosters", "parks", "gamelogs"],
    dataset_name="public",
)

print(info)

docs.title: Custom dlt Pipelines & Sources
docs.text:
For fine-grained control over incremental loading, staging credentials, and write dispositions (e.g. append vs replace):

import dlt
from retrosheetpy.sink.dlt_sink import retrosheet_source

# 1. Initialize custom dlt pipeline
pipeline = dlt.pipeline(
    pipeline_name="mlb_production_warehouse",
    destination=dlt.destinations.snowflake(),
    dataset_name="retrosheet_raw",
)

# 2. Instantiate retrosheet source for specific datasets
source = retrosheet_source(
    years=[2024],
    datasets=["events", "gamelogs", "rosters", "parks"],
)

# 3. Run pipeline with replace or append disposition
load_info = pipeline.run(source, write_disposition="replace")
print(load_info)

docs.title: Handling PostgreSQL Schemas
docs.text: [!TIP] PostgreSQL prohibits custom schemas starting with pg_. When configuring dlt, explicitly pass dataset_name="public" or a custom schema name such as dataset_name="retrosheet" to avoid schema naming conflicts.

docs.title: DuckDB Integration
docs.text: DuckDB is the recommended analytical database engine for retrosheetpy. It runs in-process with zero server setup, processes millions of rows in milliseconds using vectorized execution, and queries Parquet and PyArrow memory directly.

docs.title: Direct Ingestion (to_duckdb)
docs.text:
The to_duckdb function downloads, extracts, and streams datasets into a DuckDB database file:

import retrosheetpy as rs

# Ingest multiple seasons into a local database
rs.to_duckdb(
    path="baseball.duckdb",
    years=range(2020, 2025),
    datasets=["events", "gamelogs", "rosters", "parks"],
)

docs.title: Table Names Generated
docs.text: Dataset DuckDB Table Name events events gamelogs game_logs rosters rosters parks parks

docs.title: Querying DuckDB with SQL
docs.text:
Once ingested, you can query your data using standard SQL in Python, the DuckDB CLI, or DBeaver:

import duckdb

con = duckdb.connect("baseball.duckdb")

# Top 5 most frequent matchups
matchups = con.execute("""
    SELECT
        visiting_team,
        home_team,
        COUNT(*) AS games_played,
        ROUND(AVG(visiting_score + home_score), 2) AS avg_runs
    FROM game_logs
    GROUP BY visiting_team, home_team
    ORDER BY games_played DESC
    LIMIT 5
""").fetchdf()

print(matchups)

docs.title: Column Alignment on Pre-Existing Tables
docs.text:
If you have an established database where tables were created in advance (or contain extra columns like ingested_at or source), retrosheetpy automatically:

  1. Inspects the destination table's column names.
  2. Identifies matching columns with the incoming Retrosheet data.
  3. Performs column-aligned insertion: 
    INSERT INTO game_logs (date, visiting_team, visiting_score, ...)
SELECT date, visiting_team, visiting_score, ...
FROM _incoming_arrow;
  4. Leaves any unmapped columns set to their default or null values.
import duckdb
import retrosheetpy as rs

con = duckdb.connect("existing.duckdb")

# Pre-create table with custom subset of columns
con.execute("""
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS game_logs (
        date DATE,
        visiting_team VARCHAR,
        visiting_score SMALLINT,
        home_team VARCHAR,
        home_score SMALLINT
    )
""")

# Ingest - only matching columns are inserted!
rs.to_duckdb("existing.duckdb", years=[2024], datasets=["gamelogs"])

docs.title: Parquet & PyArrow
docs.text:
Columnar storage formats like Apache Parquet provide 10x–20x disk compression and fast read performance compared to raw CSV files.

retrosheetpy uses PyArrow internally as its core data exchange format, allowing direct export to Parquet and CSV without serialization overhead.

docs.title: Writing Parquet Files (to_parquet)
docs.text:
import retrosheetpy as rs

# Export 2024 game logs to a compressed Parquet file
rs.to_parquet(
    path="gamelogs_2024.parquet",
    dataset="gamelogs",
    years=[2024],
    compression="snappy",  # "snappy", "zstd", "gzip", "none"
)

Exporting multi-year datasets:

# Export 25 years of game logs (1990-2024) into a single Parquet file (~12 MB)
rs.to_parquet(
    path="gamelogs_1990_2024.parquet",
    dataset="gamelogs",
    years=range(1990, 2025),
    compression="zstd",
)

docs.title: Reading Back in Polars & pandas
docs.text:
Because the Parquet file contains embedded Arrow schema metadata, types (dates, integers, booleans) are preserved exactly without manual casting:

PolarspandasDuckDB 
import polars as pl

df = pl.read_parquet("gamelogs_1990_2024.parquet")
print(df.schema)

import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_parquet("gamelogs_1990_2024.parquet")
print(df.dtypes)

import duckdb

# Query the Parquet file directly with zero import time!
duckdb.sql("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM 'gamelogs_1990_2024.parquet'")

docs.title: Direct In-Memory PyArrow Tables
docs.text:
If you are building custom streaming pipelines or distributed Ray / Dask jobs, you can obtain native pyarrow.Table objects directly:

import retrosheetpy as rs

table = rs.events(year=2024, backend="arrow")

print(f"Num rows: {table.num_rows:,}")
print(f"Schema columns: {len(table.schema)}")

docs.title: SQL DDL Generator
docs.text:
When loading Retrosheet data into relational databases like PostgreSQL, DuckDB, or SQLite, having strongly-typed table definitions with primary keys, dates, and appropriate integer sizes is essential.

retrosheetpy includes a multi-dialect SQL DDL generator via rs.get_ddl().

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Generate standard DDL statements by specifying the dataset name and the target dialect:

import retrosheetpy as rs

# Generate PostgreSQL CREATE TABLE statement for game logs
print(rs.get_ddl("gamelogs", dialect="postgres"))

# Generate DuckDB CREATE TABLE statement for events
print(rs.get_ddl("events", dialect="duckdb"))

# Generate SQLite CREATE TABLE statement for rosters
print(rs.get_ddl("rosters", dialect="sqlite"))

docs.title: CLI DDL Command
docs.text:
You can also print DDL directly in your terminal to pipe into database migration scripts or psql:

# Print Postgres DDL for play-by-play events
retrosheetpy ddl --dataset events --dialect postgres

# Pipe directly into a running Postgres database
retrosheetpy ddl --dataset gamelogs --dialect postgres | psql -U postgres -d retrosheet
